why: I compared each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Check 1 asks that padLeft be exported and tests only left padding to exactly width characters, with a given fill and with the space default ("00042", "   42", "***a", "xxx"). The expect line requires all of that. Check 2 tests only that s comes back unchanged when it is already width long or longer ('abc',3; '12345',3; 'hello',2; 'xy',0). Check 3 asks that every exported function have a README section, "a markdown heading that names the function, followed by text about it". That is a fair reading of "a section for every function", not an added rule. Check 4 asks only for exit status 0 with no failing tests. The stricter points (tests existing for padLeft, multi-character fill, existing functions unchanged) all sit under the "Advisory" heading, outside any PASS or FAIL condition. No check requires exact wording, a mutation test or a branch or file-scope rule.
